title: Ahalya Is Set Free
captions: The next morning, the sages took the princes across the Ganga by boat. They stayed a night in the fine city of Vishala, and then walked on towards Mithila.
Near Mithila they came upon an old hermitage, empty and silent. “Whose ashram was this?” asked Rama. “It was the home of Sage Gautama and his wife Ahalya,” said Vishvamitra.
“They lived here in peace, doing tapas,” said the sage. “But one day, while Gautama was away, Indra, king of the devas, came disguised as Gautama and tricked Ahalya.”
“When the real Gautama returned, he was filled with anger. ‘You will live here unseen by anyone,’ he told Ahalya, ‘until Rama, son of Dasharatha, comes. Then you will be free.’”
“Then Gautama went away to the Himalaya. For thousands of years Ahalya stayed here, unseen, living only on air and doing tapas with a patient heart.”
“Rama, enter the hermitage,” said Vishvamitra. As soon as Rama stepped inside, Ahalya appeared before them, shining like a flame. Her long tapas was complete.
Rama and Lakshmana touched her feet with respect, and she welcomed them as honoured guests. Flowers rained from the sky, and Sage Gautama came home to Ahalya at last.
story: The next morning, the sages took the princes across the Ganga by boat. They stayed a night in the fine city of Vishala, then walked on towards Mithila.

Near Mithila they found an old hermitage, empty and silent. Rama asked whose ashram it was. Vishvamitra told him it had been the home of the sage Gautama and his wife Ahalya, who once lived there in peace, doing tapas.

One day, while Gautama was away, Indra, the king of the devas, came disguised as Gautama and tricked Ahalya. When the real Gautama returned, he was filled with anger. He told Ahalya that she would live there unseen by anyone until Rama, son of Dasharatha, came. Then she would be free.
Gautama went away to the Himalaya. For thousands of years Ahalya stayed alone in the hermitage, unseen, living only on air and doing tapas with a patient heart.

Vishvamitra asked Rama to enter. As soon as Rama stepped inside, Ahalya appeared before them, shining like a flame. Rama and Lakshmana touched her feet with respect, and she welcomed them as honoured guests. Flowers rained from the sky, and Sage Gautama came home to Ahalya at last.
lesson: For thousands of years Ahalya had lived alone, unseen by anyone. When Rama came, he greeted her with kindness, and he and Lakshmana bowed and touched her feet, honouring her as a great woman of tapas. In our tradition, Karuna means compassion: noticing someone who is lonely or left out, and bringing them kindness and respect. Our elders teach that a kind heart can bring light to someone who has waited a long time for it.
lesson_long: Karuna means compassion: noticing when someone is hurting, and wanting to help.

Ahalya had been alone for a very long time. When Rama came, he did not judge her or ask hard questions. He and Lakshmana bowed and touched her feet, honouring her as a great woman of tapas. Their kindness and respect ended her long wait.
Our elders teach that a kind heart can bring light to someone who has waited a long time for it. Sometimes the kindest thing we can do is simply to include someone.
tradition: In Valmiki's Ramayana, Ahalya becomes visible again when Rama arrives. In later tellings, such as the Ramcharitmanas of Tulsidas, she has been turned to stone and comes back to life at the touch of Rama's feet. Both tellings share the same truth: Rama's grace frees those who wait for him with faith.
Ahalya is remembered with great respect. She is named first among the Panchakanya, five women honoured in a traditional morning prayer.
words: the peaceful home of a sage
long, focused prayer and self discipline
five great women honoured in a morning prayer
question: Have you ever seen someone who was left out or alone? What could you do to show them kindness?
questions: Have you ever seen someone who was left out or alone? What could you do to show them kindness?
Why do you think Rama and Lakshmana touched Ahalya's feet?
How do you feel when someone includes you?
card_lesson: Ahalya had been alone and unseen for many years. Rama greeted her with kindness and touched her feet with respect. Karuna means bringing kindness to someone who feels left out.
